transcription: SUBJECTIVE:,  This 23-year-old white female presents with complaint of allergies.  She used to have allergies when she lived in Seattle but she thinks they are worse here.  In the past, she has tried Claritin, and Zyrtec.  Both worked for short time but then seemed to lose effectiveness.  She has used Allegra also.  She used that last summer and she began using it again two weeks ago.  It does not appear to be working very well.  She has used over-the-counter sprays but no prescription nasal sprays.  She does have asthma but doest not require daily medication for this and does not think it is flaring up.,MEDICATIONS: , Her only medication currently is Ortho Tri-Cyclen and the Allegra.,ALLERGIES: , She has no known medicine allergies.,OBJECTIVE:,Vitals:  Weight was 130 pounds and blood pressure 124/78.,HEENT:  Her throat was mildly erythematous without exudate.  Nasal mucosa was erythematous and swollen.  Only clear drainage was seen.  TMs were clear.,Neck:  Supple without adenopathy.,Lungs:  Clear.,ASSESSMENT:,  Allergic rhinitis.,PLAN:,1.  She will try Zyrtec instead of Allegra again.  Another option will be to use loratadine.  She does not think she has prescription coverage so that might be cheaper.,2.  Samples of Nasonex two sprays in each nostril given for three weeks.  A prescription was written as well.

CHIEF COMPLAINT:,  Achilles ruptured tendon.,HISTORY:,  Mr. XYZ is 41 years of age, who works for Chevron and lives in Angola.  He was playing basketball in Angola back last Wednesday, Month DD, YYYY, when he was driving toward the basket and felt a pop in his posterior leg.  He was seen locally and diagnosed with an Achilles tendon rupture.  He has been on crutches and has been nonweightbearing since that time.  He had no pain prior to his injury.  He has had some swelling that is mild.  He has just been on aspirin a day due to his traveling time.  Pain currently is minimal.,PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:,  Denies diabetes, cardiovascular disease, or pulmonary disease.,CURRENT MEDICATIONS:,  Malarone, which is an anti-malarial.,ALLERGIES:,  NKDA,SOCIAL HISTORY:,  He is a petroleum engineer for Chevron.  Drinks socially.  Does not use tobacco.,PHYSICAL EXAM:,  Pleasant gentleman in no acute distress.  He has some mild swelling on the right ankle and hindfoot.  He has motion that is increased into dorsiflexion.  He has good plantarflexion.  Good subtalar, Chopart and forefoot motion.  His motor function is intact although weak into plantarflexion.  Sensation is intact.  Pulses are strong.  In the prone position, he has diminished tension on the affected side.  There is some bruising around the posterior heel.  He has a palpable defect about 6-8 cm proximal to the insertion site that is tender for him.  Squeezing the calf causes no plantarflexion of the foot.,IMPRESSION:,  Right Achilles tendon rupture.,PLAN:,  Operative fixation recommended.  He would be nonweightbearing in a splint for 10 days, nonweightbearing in a dynamic brace for 4 weeks, and then a walking boot for another six weeks.

PREOPERATIVE DIAGNOSIS: , Morbid obesity.,POSTOPERATIVE DIAGNOSIS:  ,Morbid obesity.,PROCEDURE: , Laparoscopic antecolic antegastric Roux-en-Y gastric bypass with EEA anastomosis.,ANESTHESIA: , General with endotracheal intubation.,INDICATION FOR PROCEDURE: , This is a 30-year-old female, who has been overweight for many years.  She has tried many different diets, but is unsuccessful.  She has been to our Bariatric Surgery Seminar, received some handouts, and signed the consent.  The risks and benefits of the procedure have been explained to the patient.  The patient tolerated the procedure well without any complications.

PREOPERATIVE DIAGNOSES,Airway obstruction secondary to severe subglottic tracheal stenosis with foreign body in the trachea.,POSTOPERATIVE DIAGNOSES,Airway obstruction secondary to severe subglottic tracheal stenosis with foreign body in the trachea.,OPERATION PERFORMED,Neck exploration; tracheostomy; urgent flexible bronchoscopy via tracheostomy site; removal of foreign body, tracheal metallic stent material.,INDICATIONS FOR SURGERY,The patient is a 50-year-old white male with history of progressive tracheomalacia. He underwent bronchoscopy and was found to have extensive subglottic upper tracheal stenosis secondary to metallic stent granulation.,PLAN:, Removal of stents and stabilization of airway with #8 Shiley single cannula tracheostomy tube. Patient tolerated the procedure well.

CHIEF COMPLAINT:,  Urinary retention.,HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS: , This is a 66-year-old gentleman status post deceased donor kidney transplant in 12/07, who has had recurrent urinary retention issues since that time.  Cystoscopy showed obstructive BPH.  He was started on Flomax at the time of discharge.,ASSESSMENT AND PLAN:, Benign prostatic hypertrophy with recurrent urinary retention. Prescription for Flomax and Proscar for 6 months. Follow-up in 6 weeks.

CHIEF COMPLAINT:, Severe headache and visual disturbances.,HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:, This is a 45-year-old female presenting with a 3-day history of severe throbbing headache localized to the right temporal region, associated with photophobia, phonophobia, and nausea. She reports seeing flashing lights before the onset of pain. She has a history of migraines since age 20 but states this episode is more severe than usual. She denies fever, neck stiffness, or loss of consciousness.,MEDICATIONS:, Sumatriptan 50 mg PRN, Ibuprofen 400 mg PRN.,ALLERGIES:, Penicillin - rash.,PHYSICAL EXAM:, Alert and oriented x3. Cranial nerves II-XII intact. No papilledema on fundoscopic exam. No meningeal signs. Neurological exam within normal limits.,ASSESSMENT:, Migraine with aura.,PLAN:, 1. Sumatriptan 100 mg at onset of next episode. 2. Start prophylactic topiramate 25 mg nightly, titrate to 50 mg over 4 weeks. 3. Refer to neurology clinic for further evaluation. 4. MRI brain if symptoms worsen or change in character.

CHIEF COMPLAINT:, Abdominal pain and blood in stool.,HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:, This is a 58-year-old male presenting with a 2-week history of intermittent lower abdominal cramping and hematochezia. He reports 3-4 episodes of bright red blood per rectum. He denies fever, weight loss, or changes in bowel habits. Family history is significant for colon cancer in his father at age 65.,MEDICATIONS:, Lisinopril 10 mg daily, Atorvastatin 20 mg daily.,ALLERGIES:, No known drug allergies.,PHYSICAL EXAM:, Abdomen soft, mild tenderness in left lower quadrant without guarding or rigidity. Digital rectal exam reveals no masses, hemoccult positive.,ASSESSMENT:, Lower gastrointestinal bleeding, rule out colorectal neoplasm.,PLAN:, 1. Colonoscopy scheduled within 1 week. 2. CBC and coagulation studies ordered. 3. Patient instructed to return to ER if bleeding worsens or hemodynamic instability develops. 4. NPO after midnight before procedure.

CHIEF COMPLAINT:, Fatigue, weight gain, and cold intolerance.,HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:, This is a 52-year-old female presenting with a 6-month history of progressive fatigue, unexplained weight gain of 12 pounds, constipation, dry skin, hair loss, and cold intolerance. She denies palpitations, heat intolerance, or neck swelling. She has no prior thyroid history.,MEDICATIONS:, Calcium carbonate 500 mg daily.,ALLERGIES:, Sulfa - urticaria.,PHYSICAL EXAM:, Vital signs: BP 118/76, HR 58, weight 182 lbs. Skin dry and slightly thickened. Hair coarse. Thyroid non-palpable. Reflexes delayed in relaxation phase bilaterally.,LABS:, TSH 12.4 mIU/L (elevated), Free T4 0.6 ng/dL (low).,ASSESSMENT:, Primary hypothyroidism.,PLAN:, 1. Start levothyroxine 50 mcg daily. 2. Recheck TSH and Free T4 in 6 weeks. 3. Counsel patient on medication compliance and signs of over-replacement. 4. Annual thyroid panel thereafter.

CHIEF COMPLAINT:, Suspicious skin lesion on left forearm.,HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:, This is a 67-year-old male with a history of extensive sun exposure presenting with a 3-month history of a growing, irregularly pigmented lesion on the left forearm. He reports the lesion has changed in color and border over the past month. He denies pain or bleeding from the lesion. He has a history of two prior basal cell carcinomas removed from the face.,MEDICATIONS:, Metformin 500 mg twice daily, Amlodipine 5 mg daily.,ALLERGIES:, No known drug allergies.,PHYSICAL EXAM:, Lesion 1.4 cm x 1.1 cm on left volar forearm with irregular borders, asymmetric shape, and variegated pigmentation ranging from tan to dark brown with focal areas of black. No satellite lesions. No regional lymphadenopathy.,ASSESSMENT:, Suspicious pigmented lesion, rule out melanoma.,PLAN:, 1. Excisional biopsy with 2 mm margins performed today under local anesthesia. 2. Specimen sent to pathology for evaluation. 3. Patient to return in 7-10 days for results. 4. Counseled on sun protection and monthly self-skin exams.

CHIEF COMPLAINT:, Persistent low mood and inability to function at work.,HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:, This is a 34-year-old male presenting with a 4-month history of depressed mood, anhedonia, hypersomnia, decreased appetite with 8-pound weight loss, difficulty concentrating, and feelings of worthlessness. He denies suicidal ideation, hallucinations, or manic episodes. He reports increased work stress following a recent promotion. No prior psychiatric history.,MEDICATIONS:, No current medications.,ALLERGIES:, No known drug allergies.,MENTAL STATUS EXAM:, Alert, cooperative, well-groomed. Speech normal rate and volume. Mood depressed, affect constricted but reactive. No evidence of psychosis. Cognition intact. Insight and judgment good.,ASSESSMENT:, Major depressive disorder, single episode, moderate severity.,PLAN:, 1. Start sertraline 50 mg daily, increase to 100 mg after 2 weeks if tolerated. 2. Refer to cognitive behavioral therapy. 3. Safety plan discussed and provided. 4. Follow-up in 4 weeks to assess medication response. 5. Patient instructed to call crisis line or go to ER if suicidal thoughts develop.

CHIEF COMPLAINT:, Chest pain and shortness of breath on exertion.,HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:, This is a 71-year-old male with a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia presenting with a 3-week history of exertional chest pressure radiating to the left arm, associated with dyspnea on mild exertion. Symptoms resolve with rest within 5 minutes. He denies chest pain at rest, diaphoresis, or syncope. He is a former smoker with 30 pack-year history.,MEDICATIONS:, Metoprolol 25 mg daily, Atorvastatin 40 mg daily, Aspirin 81 mg daily.,ALLERGIES:, Codeine - nausea.,PHYSICAL EXAM:, BP 148/88, HR 72, regular. JVD absent. Lungs clear. Heart regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs. No peripheral edema.,EKG:, Normal sinus rhythm, no ST changes at rest.,ASSESSMENT:, Stable angina pectoris, high suspicion for coronary artery disease.,PLAN:, 1. Nuclear stress test ordered. 2. Increase Atorvastatin to 80 mg. 3. Add isosorbide mononitrate 30 mg daily. 4. Refer to cardiology for possible cardiac catheterization. 5. Strict blood pressure control. 6. Return in 2 weeks or sooner if symptoms worsen.
